name: Modern SEO - M3L2 Core 30 Gap Analysis
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 3 Core 30](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-3-core-30) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
A live demo (9:11) on a Chicago carpet cleaning client. Before building Core 30 pages, find which GBP categories and services have no matching page, which pages need optimizing, and the build order. Three steps: crawl with Screaming Frog, have Claude compare the crawl to the GBP, then double check the AI.

# Key concepts
- **What it reveals:** categories without pages, services without dedicated pages, pages to optimize, and priority order.
- **Screaming Frog** is free up to 500 URLs (per the instructor). Export internal_all.csv (Internal tab) and links_all.csv (Links tab).
- **Prompt inputs** ("Analyze Website for GBP Category & Services Silo Gaps"): both CSVs, pasted homepage content, primary and secondary GBP categories, services sorted by category, city name. He used Claude Opus 4.1 over Sonnet.
- **Prep while it runs:** filter internal_all to HTML + Indexable, review Title 1, H1, H2.
- **The AI was wrong.** It marked an existing "Area Rug Cleaning in Chicago" page as missing (it had only looked at certain directories) and claimed "high search volume" with no data. Re-prompting fixed it.
- **URL structure does not matter** (Claude kept recommending URL formats).
- **Verify everything** against the real GBP and internal_all: every suggested page must match a real category or service and not already exist.
- **Outcome:** about 45 minutes (10 to run, about 30 to check) produced 3 to 4 months of planned content.

# Steps
1. Crawl the homepage URL; export internal_all.csv and links_all.csv.
2. Paste the gap prompt into Claude; attach both files; add homepage text, categories, services, city; run.
3. Filter internal_all in Excel while it runs.
4. For every "missing" page, Ctrl+F in internal_all.
5. Tell the AI what it missed; ask it to re-audit all pages and explain what priorities are based on.
6. Re-check the final output; save it as the Core 30 roadmap.

# Notable quotes
- "You just can't trust AI output blindly."
- "This isn't something to take and start producing."

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Kim can crawl [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub) (crawling only reads the site) and pull each [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile)'s categories and services; Claude runs the analysis and Kim checks it.
- **Alphalete may hit the 500 URL free limit** (about 243 pages and posts plus images and files). Decide with Kim before paying for anything.
- Alphalete's /services/ city pages and blog posts may already cover a "missing" service, as in the demo.
- If Claude ranks pages by "search volume" without data, push back; validate volume in [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas) and Keyword Planner per Kim's rule.
- Output is a recommendation list (pages to build, pages to optimize) for Kim.

# Caveats and open questions
- The full prompt is on the course page; only partly visible on screen.
- Page counts in the demo differ (222, 237, 267) and are not explained.
- Claude's "Tier 1 priority" and title format suggestions were AI output, not instructor advice.
